caveats: PROPOSED FY2027/FY2028 budget figures from a presentation deck. Not adopted appropriations, not expenditures, not encumbrances, not cash.
The deck states 149 projects across the five-year program but prints line-item tables for only a subset, almost all FY2027-FY2028. These rows are what the document actually prints.
FY2029-FY2031 line items are not printed in this source.

Amounts are assigned to a fiscal year by column position taken from each table header, not by the order dollar signs appear. Rows whose header geometry could not be read are flagged year_unassignable and left null.

No expenditure, encumbrance, remaining-authorization, schedule, status or restriction data exists in this source. Every such field is null and must come from the adopted budget, an encumbrance report, and restriction research.
Funding-source subtotal tables are captured separately in funding_source_rows and must never be summed together with project rows.

restrictions.method: restriction_class is taken ONLY from a researched legal_basis in BeTH's 106-fund ledger or a cited statute/measure. Where BeTH's ledger records 'Not yet researched', the class here is 'unknown' and the amount is NOT redirectable for dashboard purposes. Fund type (enterprise, special revenue) is recorded as a signal but is NOT by itself treated as proof of restriction.

classes.voter_approved_tax: Parcel tax, sales tax or similar approved by voters for a stated purpose. Redirection generally requires another vote.
classes.enterprise_fund: Ratepayer money in a self-supporting fund. Generally restricted to the enterprise; Proposition 218 and bond covenants may apply.
classes.internal_service: Charges collected from other City funds to fund a specific service. Not general revenue.
classes.grant_condition: External grant with conditions and clawback risk.
classes.state_restricted: State-allocated revenue with statutory use limits (for example gas tax, vehicle registration fee).
classes.unrestricted: No identified legal restriction. Requires an affirmative citation, never an absence of evidence.
classes.unknown: Not yet researched. DEFAULT. Treated as not redirectable.

summary.headline: Of 15 CIP funding sources, BeTH has a researched legal basis for 4. None is confirmed redirectable to street rehabilitation. The honest current answer to 'how much could move to streets' is: not established, and no figure should be published until the restriction research is done.

pci.headline: Berkeley has already modelled this. BeTH reuses the City's StreetSaver-based projections rather than building a rival model, and adds the funding-restriction test the City does not publish.

assessment.question: What would it take to bring Berkeley pavement to PCI 60 or better and hold it there?
assessment.answer_status: ANSWERABLE FROM CITY DATA, with limits stated
assessment.finding: The City's own 12-year projections bracket PCI 60. The Five-Year Plan alone is projected to DECLINE to about 56 by 2038. Adding Measure FF is projected to reach about 62 by 2038. So PCI 60+ is, on the City's own modelling, roughly the outcome already purchased by the Plan plus Measure FF, at about $29.6 million a year.
assessment.the_real_gap_is_70_not_60: Berkeley's adopted goal is PCI 70 (BMC 7.11.010(K)(1)), not 60. The City estimates PCI 70 by 2036 requires about $37.6 million a year, roughly $8 million a year more than current plans provide. The funding question Berkeley actually faces is the 62-to-70 gap.

scenarios_below_60.label: Five-Year Plan baseline
scenarios_below_60.description: Only the funding in the proposed Five-Year Street Rehabilitation Plan. PCI falls from 59 to about 56 by 2038 as construction cost escalation outpaces revenue growth.
scenarios_below_60.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, p.12 (PCI Projections, Figure 1)

scenarios_at_or_above_60.label: Five-Year Plan + Measure FF
scenarios_at_or_above_60.description: Adds Measure FF funding. PCI improves from 59 to about 62 by 2038. Measure FF accounts for the entire difference between this and the baseline.
scenarios_at_or_above_60.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, p.12 (PCI Projections, Figure 1)

scenarios_at_or_above_60.label: Reach 70 by 2036, then maintain
scenarios_at_or_above_60.description: The investment level the City estimates is needed to reach PCI 70 by 2036 and hold it through 2038. About $8M a year more than the Plan and Measure FF currently provide.
scenarios_at_or_above_60.source: City of Berkeley, "Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF Plans for Fiscal Years 2027-2031", Council Action Calendar, July 7, 2026, p.12 (PCI Projections, Figure 1)

critical_caveats: These are the CITY's projections, not BeTH's. BeTH has not independently verified them and cannot, without the StreetSaver segment data.

PCI 60 as a network AVERAGE can coexist with many streets in failed condition. The City's own goal pairs PCI 70 with "no streets having a PCI below 50". A network average target without a distribution floor can be met while the worst streets decay further.
All figures assume 3% annual construction cost escalation and the Council/Measure FF revenue escalation formulas. The City notes the net effect is a modest real increase in costs relative to funding.
Annual figures are 12-year averages accounting for projected revenue growth, NOT flat annual amounts.
Reaching a level and holding it are different problems with different funding profiles.
assessment.what_beth_adds: Not a rival forecast. BeTH's contribution is to show what the City's own model implies under alternative funding, and to test whether any capital reallocation could close the roughly $8M/yr gap to PCI 70. That test is currently blocked: 0 of 15 CIP funding sources are confirmed redirectable.
